utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. I see you already half to your feet, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning. Yes, Your Honour. I wanted to report back as a housekeeping or perhaps more an administrative matter, some of the issues and concerns raised at a meeting with the Victims and Witnesses Unit, and I think that I would -- what I would ask is some guidance from the Chamber as to how we can have perhaps an approach that will facilitate the smooth bringing, assisting, and sending back of witnesses while they're here. The concern arises from the fact that witnesses have had to come and then return, without having taken the stand necessarily, perhaps because of time limitations that we believe to be given under of one set of guidelines from the Pre-Trial Conference and were not met, and accordingly, the witness either had been here too long or the order was required that another witness proceed, because if other prearranged commitments. And the result is that witnesses are coming, staying long, and then it appears that principally because of length of cross-examination, we're not able to move on the orderly method that we had anticipated, based on the factors which I have just mentioned. The two avenues of possible solution that were discussed would be either -- I guess the most obvious is try to get an understanding of what the time frame would be for cross, so that we can estimate more appropriately who should be brought up and who can be on the runway waiting to take off, so to speak, or, the other alternative would seem to be bringing fewer witnesses with, running the risk, of course, that the time frame could change and we might have a gap, where there's no one here and we'd have to try to have people on standby. The very reality -- the very real issue is that everyone has a life and needs to have enough notice to put his or her affairs in order so that he or she can get here and be here without terrible concern about having left things last minute. I don't know how the Chamber with want -- or if the Chamber wants any further input from the parties on this, but I wanted to make sure that it was relayed, that the concern is very real, and that the effect on a witness, I am -- I know this, but it was confirmed, that it is demoralising, can be, and it also renders a witness less effective if a witness has to wait extra long and perhaps ends up going back and has to return. We of course understand that there are times when the witnesses do have to leave because of their own commitments. We raise these to the Chamber. But it is the other instances that are now becoming the gravamen of this particular, as it were, complaint. If I can answer anything further or relay anything back or if perhaps a conference of a different nature is required, but I felt it obligatory to inform the Chamber and of course the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Somers. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I would just briefly like to put forward our position concerning this problem put forward by Ms. Somers. First thing is essential for this trial. The rights of the accused in this trial, the rights of Pavle Strugar, must never and in no way be prejudiced on account of procedural problems that the OTP is facing. Secondly, as to the reason why this has occurred on a number of occasions, that witnesses come here and do not manage to make it to the witness stand, as far as I understand, the OTP believes that this is for the best part the responsibility of the Defence team. We take the strongest possible exception to this. We are certainly not a source of difficulty during this trial. We must inform the Trial Chamber that we shall have no such insinuations, and we deem them unacceptable. We believe the main problem is that the OTP has been doing poorly as far as assessing the length of individual witness testimonies is concerned. They draw up new lists every week, containing up to seven or even ten witnesses per week. And by now, they should know what the average speed is of interviewing a single witness. I would just give you the most recent example of this, of a misjudgement on the part of the OTP, in terms of both the entire length of the examination of a witness, as well as the examination-in-chief by the OTP. We were given a list yesterday. We were all given a list. There is a witness who awaits continuation of our cross-examination, Mr. Grbic. The estimated length of the examination-in-chief was one hour. We all witnessed the examination-in-chief yesterday, and it went on for one hour and 48 minutes, which is 80 per cent longer than originally planned. So we believe it's a problem of planning on the part of the OTP, and by misjudging the length of their own examination, they lead to further problems, to further expenses, by having to keep the witness here in The Hague. Therefore, we would kindly ask the Trial Chamber to take no further measures that would affect the Defence, while the responsibility clearly remains with the OTP and their inability to correctly estimate the length of their own examination of witnesses. This must in no way prejudice the rights of Mr. Strugar. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It has been of concern to the Chamber since this trial commenced that the progress of hearing evidence has been slower than we anticipated and is slower than is normal in the conduct of business of the Tribunal. There has not been just one cause of this; there have been a number. And it's, I don't think, to any great advantage for each side to be pointing the finger at the other side and saying they've caused it all. It is fair to say that some problems have not been the fault of either side, but some problems have been created by each side. And the result of those is that we are well behind where we ought to have been by this time. The delay in the start of the trial had itself a very significant effect on the ordering of witnesses and disrupted considerably the initial schedules that had been put in place, both for our progress and, obviously, for those responsible for ensuring that witnesses are here. That has directly led, in at least two cases, to the need to interrupt the evidence of witnesses because they could no longer stay because of important long-term commitments to be somewhere else. We were slow in reaching them, and the time they had made available to us had elapsed before their evidence had concluded. The interruption of the evidence of a witness, for the witness to return at a later time, is of no help to anyone. It is a considerable difficulty, and we hope that can be avoided in the future. It is clear that some Prosecution witnesses have taken longer in giving their evidence in chief than was anticipated. More than one have taken something approaching double the estimated time. But what is a very significant and ongoing problem is that cross-examination has taken far longer than anticipated and has taken far longer than is normal in proceedings in the Tribunal. Both parties are aware that at the pre-trial, a very experienced Judge of the Tribunal took the view that an approximate estimate would be to allow to the Defence 60 per cent of the time that had been taken by the Prosecution in evidence in chief, that representing what, in the experience of the Tribunal, was a fair, average time to enable the cross-examination of most witnesses to be properly concluded, with all important issues dealt with but with counsel having to be very disciplined so as to not to spend time on matters that were not of importance. Now, our average has been between two and a half and three times, not 60 per cent, but getting between 200 and 300 per cent, 250 and 300 per cent of the length of time taken by witnesses in their evidence in chief. I do appreciate that with a few witnesses the cross-examination has been at about or within the 60 per cent, but so far, for the majority, the cross-examination has been very prolonged. I have made observations in the past to Mr. Rodic and Mr. Petrovic that some of the issues being pursued in cross-examination were matters that appeared not to be material, and on most occasions, that has been agreed and the cross-examination has moved on to another subject. What should be obvious is that the matter needn't have been dealt with in the first place, if it wasn't important. We cannot continue to have the length of time spent on each witness that is presently occurring. There have been some important witnesses so far, but there have been a number of others whose evidence is, by and large, routine. And in a very short time, issues of the reliability of their evidence and of whether or not they are biased can be dealt with, and for the most other part, the cross-examination has been largely simply going over their evidence and confirming it. So we will say very directly that we expect that the course of cross-examination will come to be more closely directed to the important issues, and there'll be a considerable shortening of the time spent in dealing with most of the witnesses. The Chamber made clear at the beginning, and it still holds to the view, that on important issues with an important witness, we would not curtail cross-examination. We want to ensure that the accused has every proper opportunity to test the Prosecution case, and nothing we're presently saying will change that. But unfortunately, that approach has led to time being taken on less important witnesses and less important issues that need not be spent, and in that area, the length of the hearing and the length of the cross-examination will simply have to be reduced. Once again, I invite Defence counsel to give serious consideration when they are preparing their cross-examination to whether each matter really needs to be dealt with, because if it doesn't, it should be passed over entirely or dealt with quickly, with one or two questions. The Chamber is well able to pick up the drift and significance of your questioning, as I think has been apparent on a number of occasions already. So you don't need to dwell on it, on and on on the topic, once you've got your message home. That way, I hope we can see a considerable reduction in the length of cross-examination. If that does not eventuate, the Chamber will have to start the prospect or consider the prospect of imposing time limitations to be normally observed unless the Chamber specifically in a case allows some greater time. So we invite counsel for the Defence to give very close attention to the time being spent on cross-examination, because we simply cannot afford the time that is being spent to this stage of the trial. If that continues, the length of this trial will just go out to a totally unnecessary and undesirable length. It is also apparent to the Chamber that the Prosecution is too eager in its estimate of the time a witness will take. This has been so from the early stages. We have detected a slight easing of that eagerness and a slightly more realistic spacing in the latest lists, but even so, they may still be a little too eager. You will appreciate that from the outset we have made it clear that we are not applying any sort of 60 per cent cross rule, and therefore, estimates based on that will not hold and are not holding, and you need to lengthen out with a relatively simple monitoring. We ought not reach the stage where we simply lose a day because there's no witness here. We may well find that we finish half an hour or an hour early in one session before the next witness is available, but that should be all. If the two important measures that we have indicated are observed in the future, that is, that the Defence take a more realistic time in cross-examination and the Prosecution allows a more realistic estimate of the time each witness will take, I think the problems of which we're conscious that are being experienced by the witness unit will be greatly diminished, and they will be able to manage things in a way which they are more comfortable with. With those observations, thank you for bringing the matter to our attention at this point, Ms. Somers, and we hope that there will be a significant improvement from all viewpoints in the future.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. I will of course take all of this discussion back to the liaison person from the investigative team and to the victim witness liaison person, and we will, based on, as always happens in trial, issues arise which perhaps make us readjust what might be asked of witnesses and have to readjust timing. But we accept certainly that it is incumbent on us to be as crisp and narrow as possible, and where we can trim sufficiently, we will do so. Some witnesses really are so restricted in the questioning; for example, death issues, did someone die there or not. I think these are issues that we can try to keep very, very narrow and I hope we will get the cooperation, I'm sure that we will get the cooperation of my learned friends opposite. And if there are any issues on perhaps scaling back of how many people are physically present in The Hague with the idea of having persons from the region on standby then we'll report back through the legal officer of this proposal as well. This may well be one possible solution until we get a rhythm that is more realistic. Thank you very much. With your indulgence, I would leave the Prosecution table to my very able colleague, Mr. Weiner. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, and perhaps we might bring Mr. Grbic in now. Thank you. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour -- [In English] May I ask you just for a second. I have only a sentence to say. [Interpretation] The first thing that I would like to point out is to actually confirm something that Ms. Somers said. As far as I can tell by looking at the lists, very soon witnesses will be coming that the Defence team will have no questions at all to ask of, except to thank them for being here and expressing our deepest regret at the loss that they suffered. Some of these witness will take maybe up to five minutes in cross-examination, no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another thing that we wish to say is of a more practical nature. There is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a practical problem which we will be facing before the end of this week. Today we must complete our cross-examination of the witness who has just been brought into the courtroom, and we have two other witnesses that may take up to three hours each on examination-in-chief. This in itself is not realistic. I'm not sure how we can deal with this over the following two days, in view of the fact that Mr. Pringle has to meet his schedule and complete his testimony by Friday. Lucijana Peko of the OTP claims up to three hours; Pringle up to three hours; Witness Mustac, one hour. We are just looking at the examination-in-chief, so in this way we would only be having examination-in-chief until the end of this week. I have expressed this concern to my learned friends and colleagues from the OTP on Monday when we talked. I'm not sure what solution they have managed to come up with. If you like, I can show you the schedule again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No. No need, Mr. Petrovic. We've got it right here. It will be for counsel to discuss the order of witnesses. There are two types of problem that can be encountered, of course. One is where a witness comes without notice, something that can cause particular problem for the Defence. That isn't the issue here. The issue here is whether you have notice of too many witnesses. The solution there is that the Office of the Prosecutor will have to decide which witnesses they are going to call of those that are on the list, and will tell you, I am sure, the moment decisions have been made, which witnesses are going to be called for the balance of this week. But I agree with you; all that are on the list cannot be dealt with during the remaining part of this week. We will have Mr. Grbic in. [The witness entered court

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Grbic. And I'm sorry you came in and went out and came in again. We got the timing wrong. May I remind you of the affirmation you took to tell the truth at the beginning. That's still effective. Cross-examination, Mr. Petrovic, continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will try to fully comply with everything that the Chamber has just said. Cross-examined by Mr. Petrovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Grbic. I will ask you some more questions now, questions about issues that were, for the main part, brought up yesterday. The last thing we talked about was Srdj, the hill, and Croatian defenders on top of the hill. Tell me, please: Between the Old Town itself and Srdj, what is the distance between the edge of the Old Town and where the slopes start rising towards Srdj?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Srdj itself, the height is approximately 450 metres, plus the 50 metres from the sea, so all in all, maybe about 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the eastern town walls and Srdj?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think about 400 metres, perhaps a little more, since it is sloped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the INA oil company building is located in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the police headquarters are?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where? Can you tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's midway between Dubrovnik, the Old Town, and Gruz, to the left of the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between Dubrovnik and Gruz, you mean between the Old Town and Gruz?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the distance between Pile and Gruz?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any uniformed persons inside the Old Town of Dubrovnik in October, November, and December, the time period we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My apologies. Your answer was no?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In those three months did you ever see in Dubrovnik any members of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any members of the Croatian army outside the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday, or you repeated on a number of different occasions, that -- or rather, my apologies. Did you hear about any members of the Croatian army being inside the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear exactly where they were located?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could only make an assumption that they were on Srdj and in the surroundings, but we couldn't actually see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please specify where in the surroundings? On Srdj and which surroundings are you referring to? The surroundings of what?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on, we realised, while watching video footage, that they were in the Gradac park, in the Bogisicevo [phoen] park near Glavica, and people also said that they were up near St. Blaise, Gorica, where the meteorological service is based, in Lapad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain where this park -- Gradac Park is?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's just opposite the way from the Lovrijenac fort, to the west. The distance to the town itself is about 800 metres, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Chamber what is the difference distance between the park and the Lovrijenac fort?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think about 30 or 40 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Chamber what is the distance between the Gradac park and the old hospital at Boninovo?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Gradac park borders on the green belt which surrounds the old hospital at Boninovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is the Bogisic [phoen] park in relation to the old hospital?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's to the north, on an elevation behind the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of metres, how far do you think it is from the old hospital at Boninovo?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance might be about five or six hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Gradac park, from the Boninovo hospital?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I had the Bogisic park in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It may have been my mistake, please. The Bogisic park and the old hospital?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between five and six hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is the Glavica in relation to the Bogisic park?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's part of the park. It's just that Ilijina Glavica is both the park and the surrounding area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see in the Gradac park?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see anything at the time. It was only later that I had occasion to see what had been recorded on a videotape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this a videotape from the period of time that we are referring to, October, November, and December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But I didn't have the tape at the time. I brought it with me here to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hand the tape over to my learned friends from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You handed it over to them upon your arrival here several days ago?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, what exactly can you see on that tape?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a civilian putting a small mortar shell into a barrel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you actually see this mortar shell being fired from this barrel of a gun?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you can see him firing the first shell and then he kisses the second shell and places it in the barrel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see the civilian moving around with this mortar in the footage?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just for a brief while, because he had to swerve to avoid the explosion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just tell us what this mortar looked like? You're no expert in the field, but you are an expert in visual recollection of things. So can you tell us what it looks like?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it's the 120-millimetre one. I think it's the 80 or 85-millimetre one. It's the smaller mortar, not the bigger one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How does it look? Just briefly.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a long barrel with some sort of a pedestal and two pegs in front that keep it pinned to the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that a civilian fired a shell and kissed another?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your conclusion that he was a civilian because he was wearing plain clothes [As interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the only conclusion that I could draw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other people there?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. You can't see anyone else in the footage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long is this footage?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very short.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any other recordings from the time?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is footage from the Gradac Park.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us first distinguish between these two. The footage that we've been talking about so far, that's the Bogisic park?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you see in the footage from the Gradac park?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a pine tree, a very large pine tree. There is a round fish pond. And just by looking at it in a cursory manner, I think there is the ZIS gun lying next to it, Russian production, I believe. I'm not sure about this, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please give us a description of that weapon, what you saw in the footage, at least? I'm not asking you for an expert opinion or description, but I know that you are -- you must be very good at visual recollection of things.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The barrel is slightly long and reinforced and tapering towards the end. It was fortified at the back too, to keep it firm, to keep it stable. And the colour was SMB or olive-green.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said it was placed near a tree?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see that clearly in the footage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there people around the weapon?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a young man wearing civilian clothes. I think he was carrying a camera or something. He ran from the weapon to the person who was recording the scene.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain why he ran in this direction?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure how the young man got to be there in the first place. But then he took a path to the left, an asphalt path leading down into town, and that's where the recording ends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long is this footage?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one's a bit longer than the one that was taken in the Bogisic park.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see anyone else in this footage aside from this young man?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one. Well, now that I think about it, there's a man holding a tree branch, trying to put out a fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the weapon, is there any other piece of military equipment to be seen in the footage, maybe a box with ammunition or something like that?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you can't see anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This young man standing near the weapon, is he also wearing civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can only see him moving away from the weapon in the footage. I don't know where he had come from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he's also wearing civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any other footage from that period?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We do have a tape of a small lorry where a three-barreled machine-gun was mounted, and I suppose that's an anti-aircraft gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a three-barreled anti-aircraft gun?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know whether it's anti-aircraft, but I think that such kind of weapon is used for those purposes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe this vehicle to us? Do you know what the make of it was?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was a civilian vehicle, and the footage is a very short one, and it's on the same tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any persons in the footage?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, but right now I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anyone who is part of the crew with this weapon?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice any such person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you recognise part of the town where the videotape was shot?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently, outside the town, because there are some houses uphill and there's a road. It's a close-up footage, so you couldn't see any background.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that it was not taken inside the Old Town. Is it taken -- was it taken in Dubrovnik at all?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What exactly can you see? What kind of buildings can you see?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Modern buildings and some shrubbery, probably cypress trees. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what colour is this civilian vehicle?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not olive-drab. Only the weapon was of that colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the colour of the lorry?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most certainly not military one. If it had been of the same colour as the weapon, then you might say that it belonged to the military, but apparently it was different. So you can see that on the tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me how big is this lorry?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We couldn't see the whole of the lorry. We just saw pieces of the image with those barrels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, when you say -- when we both use the word "lorry," it's not a big truck; it's something smaller than a big truck?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was my impression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please: How long were those three barrels that you can see on the tape?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately two metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me: Looking from Ploce towards the town, the passage that leads from Ploce to town, was it possible before the war for delivery vans or pick-up trucks to pass through this passage?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were allowed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that refer the same to the gate on the Pile? There is a ramp there that can allow the passage of some smaller vehicles? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only ambulances were allowed to go through that passage, but at a slow pace, because this passage is at a right -- at 90-degrees angle, and for that reason it had never been used for delivery vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I remember correctly, an ambulance could pass easily by turning to the left and then to the right?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the same situation now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you obtain these videotapes that you are now discussing?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a compilation of video footage made by some 15 domestic and foreign photographers, and it has been compiled by Mr. Benic [phoen], who is a TV journalist from the Dubrovnik television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the total duration of the tape?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe even 90 minutes, but certainly more than one hour. I'm not sure. But it's a long tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hand over this whole videotape to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you reviewed the whole tape?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it broadcast anywhere publicly? Can you remember, was it broadcast on any of the TV channels or in any other way?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only pieces from that tape were broadcast, but I don't know whether the entire tape has ever been broadcast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise that I'm using a different word for "broadcast" than the one that you use. What else can one see on that tape?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are lots of things, including the footage made by the Belgrade television and the Montenegrin television, in addition to the footage made by foreign photographers. Because when you look on the credits at the end of the tape, you can see the names of the people who were involved in the making of this tape. They were lodged in the Argentina hotel and from there they could shoot the town area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us just briefly tackle another subject. Several times you said yesterday that on the slope of Srdj, as you say, between Zarkovica and Srdj, you could see the silhouettes.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe for me once again how they looked like?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We know how the olive-drab uniform looks like. It's dark green. And given the fact that the backdrop were white rocks, without any shrubbery on it, you could very clearly distinguish them against this backdrop. Being a painter, I'm very good at perceiving these things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your window, as it was -- the window facing the west; am I right [As interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in your estimate, how far is your window to the Srdj slopes?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 400 metres that I already mentioned, plus another 150 or so. So if the width of the town is 300 metres, my house is situated somewhere in the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's the total of some 600 or 700 metres in a straight line. How do you know -- or did you know who those silhouettes were?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But they were not on this position that was in my view. They were more to the east.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You could see silhouettes from the town?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see the silhouettes from my window. I said yesterday that we could see them from the town harbour. These silhouettes were visible to the east from the town between Srdj and Grabovica, and that's Zarkovica, and that's a totally different area which I cannot see from my window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you were on Porporela, how long is the distance?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Much longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between 700 or 800 metres?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: Who were those people, those silhouettes?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So if you see that they are all uniformly dressed in dark-green clothes and with dark-green hats, hats on their heads, you just wouldn't assume that those were civilians. And I'm quite sure that Croatian forces were not at this position, because that is to the east from the Srdj peak, towards Zarkovica. You have bare rocks there, and in the middle there is the village of Bosanka. It's a very steep slope.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say exactly at what of these features the Croatian forces were deployed and where the forces of the opposite side were deployed?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite clear, because our forces only held the very peak of Srdj. Everything outside that area were not our forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in your statement, or in the addendum to your statement that you submitted to Mr. Weiner upon your arrival here in The Hague, you could see that those silhouettes were moving from Zarkovica towards Srdj. You didn't explain who those people were who were deployed or moving between Zarkovica and Srdj. In which direction were they moving? What did they do?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see quite clearly from the tape that there was a silhouette of a tank moving towards the fortress. So you can see it intermittently in the tape. You can see the barrel of the tank. And it was moving much faster than the silhouettes were moving, the ones that we had previously seen on the rocks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So since you knew the deployment of the defenders and of the other forces, you could draw a conclusion who was who. Therefore, I may conclude that you precisely know where the Croatian defenders were located and where the JNA was.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If everybody said -- everybody said that our defenders were only on Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we try to -- if we look at your statement made in the year 2000, plus your additional explanation, and when you add to that what we heard from you yesterday, when you discussed or explained to this Chamber what was happening, could you make a distinction between what you saw on the tape and what you saw yourself? So can you clearly distinguish between the two?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I specifically pointed out this to Mr. Weiner, by saying that what I saw on the tape was not possible for me to see personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell us specifically yesterday: This is what I saw in the tape, this is what I experienced personally, and this is what I heard from third persons? Or you didn't make this distinction at all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There was no discussion in the examination-in-chief of the tapes, which are just public broadcasts that he's copied, which are just news broadcasts from Belgrade, Sarajevo, Montenegro, wherever, Zagreb. There was no discussion of the tapes. He was asked yesterday about his own observations, and also what he had heard, period. There was no discussion of the tapes. I just want to make that very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That may help you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, although I beg to differ, I wouldn't dwell on this matter any longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you just described you saw on the tape?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Through your three-month experience, and you know which three months I'm referring to, did you ever hear any -- from the place where you were located, did you hear any operation or any shooting or firing from these parks that we mentioned? Had you ever heard any shooting coming from the town into any direction?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not during those three months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have no experience of that?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you distinguish, then, between the sound coming from Zarkovica, for example, or the sound coming from Babin Kuk, for instance? Were you able to distinguish between the sound heard coming from Bosanka or, for example, from Lapad?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: You told us yesterday that due to all those circumstances in which you lived at the time during those three months in Dubrovnik in the Old Town, you walked around very often in order to ease the pressure that you had to endure. Can you tell us which routes you took in your walks? Please don't repeat what you already said yesterday. You told us that you walked on Porporela, through the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go up to Porporela, but I went to the city harbour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you walked down your street, Od Puca, you walked on Stradun. During those walks, and during those three months, did you ever leave the perimeter of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: Where did you go and how many times you went there?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first went towards the west, because the eastern part of the town, facing Ploce, was very much open to the positions on Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went through the Pile gate on Ante Starcevic Street?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to Persijane. I told you yesterday this is a plateau on Pile where there's a fountain and from where you can see the Lovrijenac fortress and the sea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you leave the Old Town? Did you do that on a daily basis or once a week?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We left the Old Town in November, after those three horrible days on the 10th, 11th, and the 12th, when the town was shelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: How far did you go? Did you go just as far as Pile or did you go further to the west?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went past the Imperijal hotel, whose roof was burned. Then we took the street Petra Zrinskoga, which is north towards the Srdj, because there are three so-called corners, in fact, three parallel streets, and we went as far as the farthest third street, with the intention of looking for some edible plants in order to enrich our diet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this walk, did you go behind the hotel or you just went as far as the entrance?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went only as far as the entrance to the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you walked down this route, did you see any members of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you always go through the eastern gate on Ploce?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During all these three months, did you see any armed individuals carrying gun or rifle [As interpreted] in the town?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen any policemen?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen any members of the civilian protection?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any civilians carrying pistols? Did you see any civilian carrying guns?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know anyone who was a member of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As someone who has been living in Dubrovnik for a long time, did you know a lot of people at all?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How is it possible, then -- or did you hear that anyone was a member of these forces?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean in 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you properly, in 1991, you've never heard of anyone being a member of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were prisoners there. We didn't have much contacts. I told you that we left the town very rarely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were many people from outside of town, many refugees. People were telling about what was going on and discussing whether the JNA was going to enter the town, whether Dubrovnik would manage to defend itself. Were you not interested to know if there was anyone prepared to defend the town?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I was interested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get any answer to these questions that you would like to know?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer was that we were surrounded by major armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you about three names now. For example, General Nojko Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We'd heard about him being a commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me precisely what you heard. The commander of what?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the commander of a more general military nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was he commander? The defence of Dubrovnik or the general area? What did he do?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he commanded the defence of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, didn't you wonder if there was a commander? Probably this commander led some forces, some soldiers. Wasn't that a logical question to ask? Wasn't that a logical thing to wonder?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It strikes me as logical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was the answer?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were prisoners inside the town, we civilians. We had no contact with this gentleman you've referred to, or anyone else, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you knew there was a commander, you knew there was a unit, but you never wanted to know, you never wondered whether the unit had any soldiers, whether it in fact existed. You learned that there was a commander. You seem a man of broad interests and an educated man. It strikes me as strange that you didn't ask yourself any questions about that at the time. I find that difficult to believe.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, do your best. Try to believe what I'm telling you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you listen to Radio Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We all did. That was our only link with the outside world.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Radio Dubrovnik cover the activities of the Croatian army in the area of Dubrovnik town, or rather, the activities of the Croatian army in terms of defending the town, in the general town area?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They mostly talked about victims, water, food, electricity supply, how refugees travelled, when a ship would arrive. They mostly covered the essentials, what was really important for the life of those civilians imprisoned inside the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Radio Dubrovnik cover JNA attacks on Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Radio Dubrovnik cover the resistance of the town to JNA units? Did they try to soothe the population? Did they try to provide some explanation of what was going on?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They wanted to soothe people's minds, but if they had said anything publicly about the Croatian units, they would have been disclosing military secrets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they, for example, say: The Croatian defenders repelled an attack from this or that position? Did you hear anything like that?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. As I said, Radio Dubrovnik mostly covered issues to do with the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you distinguish between an incendiary shell and one that is not an incendiary shell?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The incendiary shell leaves an orange trail where it explodes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a peculiar smell that you associate with an incendiary shell?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the smell only lasts very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object to this. Your Honour, we have military experts who are going to testify. I assume they will be bringing military experts that will testify. This man is an artist. He is not an expert in projectiles, and he should not be offering opinions in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, please. First of all, I am really quite surprised that Mr. Weiner should try to interrupt me with a remark of this nature. The witness testified for the whole day yesterday that unfortunately what happened at his home was that a projectile had exploded, an incendiary projectile, he said explicitly. I'm not asking him about the specifics of a mortar shell. I'm just asking him about what he experienced, what he felt. He described for us the kind of flame and the effect that the shell had. I just want to know whether he noticed a peculiar smell by which this incendiary shell would have been different from any other shell. I think my questions address directly issues elicited by Mr. Weiner during his examination-in-chief yesterday, and the witness did, after all, provide a very specific description of the shell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Petrovic. Thank you, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sense any peculiar smell after this incendiary shell exploded?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, we had taken shelter in a room that was between the kitchen and the living room. We were ten steps away from the attic where the shell exploded. If it's a phosphorescence shell, then obviously there's a hideous smell spreading. And the smoke itself from the burning. It depends on where exactly the shell lands. It landed on wood and the wood caught fire in this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You provide very detailed and specific accounts of things that happened. That, after all, is your trait. As for sensory perception, what sort of a smell was it?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a bitter smell. It makes you choke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Lovrijenac fort, the fortress that we referred to yesterday, is it part of the historical heritage of the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not located within the town walls. It is about 50 metres from the town walls, on an isolated rock. It sits on top of an isolated rock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it is part of the historical heritage of the town itself?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You noticed that the fort had been damaged. You said there was damage to the stones or the rocks.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The rocks just underneath the fort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the other side, the north-west? Now we're talking about the south-west. There's the Old Town to the south-west -- to the south-east.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the north-west, there is the Gradac Park; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far from the north-western face of the fort itself in terms of distance?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly 40 metres, I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you saw an armoured vehicle, a homemade, a hand-made armoured vehicle moving. What did it look like?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw it on the tape that I brought with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see it? Did you manage to identify the vehicle's route when you saw the tape?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the people that were there were bringing a wounded man into the vehicle. He had a cast around his right leg. The leg must have been broken. And they took great care in placing the person inside the vehicle. Someone is talking to the driver, and from this conversation you can gather that this vehicle was only used to transport the wounded and food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said they were bringing a wounded person inside the vehicle. Where was the door of this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a hand-made, a homemade vehicle, made from sheets of iron welded together, roughly speaking, an armoured vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the upper side of this vehicle, did you see a weapon mounted there?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It had sloping sides, a protected lorry, a rather small one, covered in iron sheets to protect the inside of the vehicle from being hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw that they were putting a wounded man inside?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could they, for example, be placing inside the vehicle crates containing food or anything like that, ammunition perhaps?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this would have been possible, yes, but in this footage you can hear them say: Watch out. Watch out for the tree. Because the man had a plaster cast, so they wanted to avoid further damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown Prosecution document number P24, just to verify if it's the same vehicle that the witness has now been telling us about. [In English] Can you put that on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please have a look. This photograph that's displayed on your monitor, is this the vehicle we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if this still was taken from the video footage or if this is a special photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a different photograph. It's not from the footage.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that case, I'm not familiar with this image.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's not the same vehicle?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen this particular photo. I only saw the video footage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you say that this vehicle - please look carefully - that this vehicle is different from the one that you saw?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw part of that vehicle, some footage from inside the vehicle when they were bringing the wounded man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please have a careful look. This part of town, where was this recorded? We are in Dubrovnik, but where precisely? Can you identify the exact spot?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see palm trees. I can't see a single detail that would betray the exact location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you look at the building in the background.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building, four windows, a small roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... [In English] the witness. Can he take a look directly at the photo, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you find it easier now that you have the photo in your hands?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't identify the house in the background. There's a small roof, four windows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You can't identify it. That's fair enough.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see civilian cars, buses, in the background, but I don't think I can identify the location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll no longer be requiring this photograph. Thank you very much. Yesterday you described for us, on several occasions when you spoke about what happened in October, what you called the first attack, in the month of October, you described for us the peculiar sound. You described for us the situation. A shell, as you said, had hit the Rupe Museum, and then the next shell came. You heard the peculiar whizzing sound, very striking.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It must have left a very strong impression on you from that period of time?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because those were the first shells to land on Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you not find it important, as something to point out to the investigators when you talked to them in September 2000?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not lead me there with their questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did tell them about the Rupe Museum. That was probably the strongest impression you had on that day. How come you didn't tell the investigator about your strongest impression?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the investigator wanted us to just go through it very quickly and to move on. As we had not been briefed for this interview, we had not been prepared, it was easy to leave things out, to pass things over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's try to do it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just have a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday about the bullet. You were moving along, and the bullet ricochetted against the bishop's palace. Where was this?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was at Count Damjan and Junje [phoen] Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your conclusion was that the bullet came from a sniper?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a rifle bullet. That was obvious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A little later, you entered the town and another bullet hit a scaffolding?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My sister and I had just turned the corner and a bullet rang out against a metal piece of the scaffolding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that also a sniper?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume it was from the same position, the bullet had been fired from the same position when it ricochetted, and it flew back in the same direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your impression was that someone was targeting you specifically?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not the only person in that area, so they may as well have been targeting someone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it your impression that any of the people surrounding you were being specifically targeted, people in the area? You can answer my question now.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was evident that human beings were being targeted. If you fire a bullet at a town wall, that obviously doesn't make much sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were targeting you, or some of the people in the area?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That must be a dreadful experience.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, quite inconvenient.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us why you didn't tell the investigator about this horrible experience when you talked to them in September.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must repeat myself: I was not able to recollect all the details at that time. He didn't even insist on asking these same questions that you're asking me now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, on that occasion you told the investigator, for example, the following -- that's exactly what your statement says. You told him about something that was outside your own experience, something that was hearsay. You said that Mr. Toni Kalcic had been shot. You told the investigators about this. You believed it was important, even though you didn't personally witness this or were in any other way involved to what happened to Mr. Kalcic. But you left out the fact that you yourself had been sniped at. Why was that?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because my neighbour, Mr. Kalcic, is a well-known person, so I thought it was important to mention that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't you think that recounting your horrible personal experiences was more important?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we personally were not hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I understand, you are a well-known person there, and if you had been a target of the sniper, I don't see that there is anything more important to tell the investigator than that.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, he didn't ask me to provide details in terms that -- whether there was any similar case than the one with Mr. Kalcic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the first thing that comes into your mind is Mr. Kalcic and then yourself?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Because Mr. Kalcic was hit in his lower leg, and I think that was a serious wound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So why didn't you tell to the investigator about the incident when you were standing at the door facing the aquarium, when another man standing next to you was shot in the palm of his hand? You were personally witnessing the whole incident, and that's what you told us yesterday. So you personally saw a person standing 50 centimetres away from you being shot by a sniper.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't tell the investigator about this incident because it was impossible to cover all the horrendous things that happened in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Chamber, quite justifiably, warned me not to ask you about any events that took place in the nineteenth century, in the twentieth century, which took more than two pages in your statement. However, your personal experience of seeing a man being shot next to you was never mentioned in your statement.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The issue is that this statement contains what the translator said and what the investigator wrote down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling me, then, that the investigator was more interested to hear about the Serbian nineteenth-century poets than about your experience when you were a target of a sniper?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection. He can't answer what the investigator was interested in. It's outside the scope of his knowledge, as is the investigator's decisions to ask certain questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, there's a lot in what Mr. Weiner is putting in that objection. I think you must accept the evidence of the witness when he says: Well, I answered what I was asked by the investigator. You've already got from him that he didn't volunteer the personal attack on himself, if that's what it was. That's clear already. And he's saying he wasn't asked about this by the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the investigator ask you to tell him about the Serbian nineteenth-century poets?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me about the development and the political situation that prevailed and which resulted eventually in this attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the investigator ask you about Josip Broz Tito and about what happened after his death?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About general political situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ask you about the Serbian church on Gunduliceva Poljana?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This church is not on Gunduliceva Poljana.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ask you about the Serbian church?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me about many things. Therefore, what I replied was apparently in answer to the investigator's question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, he did ask you when the Serbian church was built?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Otherwise, I wouldn't have any specific reason to speak about this matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ask you about sniper-shooting incidents in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, since I mentioned Mr. Kalcic, and it's apparent that that was being discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in conclusion, he asked you about the sniper-shooting incident, you told about the experience of Mr. Kalcic, but you didn't tell him about your personal experience; am I right?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't recorded in writing, and I would like to reiterate here that I didn't have an opportunity then to look at this text, which was made from the translation done by the interpreter and written down by the investigator and which I only saw now in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us that you had been read this statement.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were able to hear what the statement was about?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was read to me and what is written is quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask the witness a couple of questions more, but I would like to do it, with your permission, after a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the first break, then, now, Mr. Petrovic. It will be for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Before I begin with the questioning of the witness, I would first like to inform you that I had a discussion with my learned colleague Weiner over the break and that we agreed that in one or two days, Mr. Weiner will tender this video cassette that had been handed to him by the witness. Therefore, we managed to resolve one important issue in this way. If I may, now I would pose a couple of more questions to the witness, and with that, I would conclude and not waste any more time of the Chamber and of the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Grbic, I would like to take you back to the 6th of December, 1991. Could you kindly tell me: When was the first time that you heard explosion?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was at 10 minutes to 6.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these explosions distant?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suppose you were asleep, so maybe my question is superfluous. Could you locate where the explosions were coming?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. We were woken up by the explosions, and we understood that they were coming from the eastern parts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did those distant detonations last?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those explosions were continuous and lasted until the moment that I went to my window at 7.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you want to say that these explosions lasted between 10 to 6.00, when you woke up, until 7.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and they were getting closer and closer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you had seen what had been happening on Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see? I heard about the cross and it's part of your evidence, but what else did you see?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shells were being exploded around the fort, within my vision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you -- which side of the fort. Are you referring towards Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. I couldn't see that part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that there was a very strong wind on that day.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, an easterly wind, which we called Levanat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could you tell that?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because those -- the smoke was very swiftly moved towards the west.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the smoke was swiftly dispersed, and therefore, that was a very strong wind?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the shelling exactly stop?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shelling subsided at around 1.00 p.m., when three of my acquaintances took my paintings from my gallery on the ground floor of my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you again -- did you still hear those distant detonations?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But we could tell that they were not so very near, and therefore, they decided to go to my gallery and take my paintings to Mr. Obad's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, could you tell from which direction, judging by the sound, did the explosions come?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They always came from the east.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, did you hear any sound of explosion coming from the north or west?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between October and late December, you mentioned yesterday that these events took place on one day in October. Can you please remind me? Because you said the whole event started on the 1st of October.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then the Rupe Museum, Museum Rupe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. We are overlapping, so I will try to phrase the question in a manner that you can directly respond to. Therefore, the event that you describe in October took place on the 25th October and involved the Rupe Museum?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On or about the 25th of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were three days --

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't mention the Pecar house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It all happened on the same day?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, or thereabouts. My memory may not be quite accurate, but that was certainly towards the end of that month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just let me remind you that you very decisively said that this event happened on the same day, but these events were a couple of minutes apart.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had different views, one from my west window and one from the east window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that the events involving the Pecar house and the museum Rupe were minutes apart.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, not minutes. As I told you, my sister and I were in the street. She was looking at the shop window. And it took some time for us to go back home. So these two events were not minutes apart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you quite sure that that was on that same day or are you not sure?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you now that you have made me wonder now and doubtful. But these events were very close to each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move now to November, the three days in November and one day in December.

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the most horrible day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So all these incidents in fact happened within the total of five days; am I right? One day in October, three days in November, and one in December?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was what I have the strongest impression of and that I and my family felt the most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: On the 6th of December, when you left your house, you said yesterday that at that very moment, shells were landing nearby; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they landing on some buildings or on streets?

utterances.speaker: IVO GRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
